PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: We have 10 cranes that will be used with the Barge Crane DB Wotan being the tallest governing crane with the highest elevation above sea level of 324 ft the description of them all is below: nDB Wotan – This derrick barge would primarily be operating at terminal 1 to the south but would also be at North Site(NES) (where the 4600 ringer is set up) from time to time. The Wotan has 240’ of boom and the crane is off the deck of the barge a substantial amount. Total height to top of boom from water surface is ~ 289’. If there is a king high tide of 35’ and the crane is boomed all the way up there is a potential for the boom tip to be at an elevation of +324’ EL. nDB Valhalla – This derrick barge will also be primarily operating at Terminal 1 but will also make visits at NES by the 4600. Total height of boom tip from water surface is 217’. With a king tide & high boom we are looking at +252’ EL. nDB Viking – Same info as for the Wotan & Viking for location on site. Total height of boom tip from water surface is 182’. With a king tide & high boom we are looking at +217’ EL. nManitowoc 4600 Ringer - The crane will be fixed and sitting on a built-out relieving platform at NES  top of concrete pad is +36’ Elevation. Crane is a 4600 ringer with 220’ of boom. If it is boomed all the way up the tip sheave is approximately 245’ off the ground surface. With a platform height of +36’ EL and the 245’ to top of sheave  maximum boom tip elevation is +281’ EL. n100 Ton Grove Rough Terrain or similar – We will have a couple 100 ton rough terrain cranes supporting the work at all locations. With the boom all the way out it is approiamtely 170’ off the ground surface. This would put the highest elevation at ~ +210’ EL. nShuttlelifts – These will primarily operate at NES. Total height of lift is 61’. Total elevation with ground surface is ~ +101’ EL.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Port of Anchorage North Site

All guy wire anchors will remain well clear of the perimeter fence and boat ramp access.nnPower Supply:nThe trailer will be powered by an adjacent Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project is for the construction of a new groundwater supply well and wellhouse for the Village's public water distribution system. For the observation wells  the drill rig will be up for approximately 2 days and will not be taken down until construction is finished. For the Test Well  a drill rig and a crane will be up for approximately 2 weeks and will not be taken down until construction is complete.  A crane will come back to the Test Well approximately 3 months after construction of the Wells are complete  in order to install the Test Well Pump. The crane similarly will be approximately 40' tall and could be up for approximately 5 days before it is taken down. We intend to put the project out to public bid in January 2025  and construction may span over approximately 4-6 months. There will be initial construction early in the project  then approximately 3 months later the crane will come back to the site and finish the project.

All structures between the AIR Substation and 0808-72 DE will be replaced with a combination of Steel Monopoles and H-frame structures resting on drilled shafts  direct embeds  and piles foundations.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The project is located along the existing transmission right-of-way  starting at the Airport Substation. From there  the line crosses MN Highway 5 heading southeast and continues into Fort Snelling State Park. Within the park  the line splits into two branches  one going north and the other south. The rebuild of the line will occur only between structures 72 and 61A.

The rebuild of the line will occur only between structures 72 and 61A.

STRUCTURE NAME: New Parking Garage - SE Tower Crane
PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The tower crane is needed for the construction of a new parking garage as part of the new terminal construction at CMH. The tower crane will mostly support the construction of the elevated concrete decks and steel reinforcing. It is anticipated to be flagged and lit. Coordination with local ATCT and Airport Operations to ensure any construction lighting does not conflict with Airport Operations. A separate submission has been made for the mobile crane that will support the erection of this tower crane.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The Tower crane is planned to be situated between two parallel runways: Runway 10L-28R and 10R-28L at CMH. The site location is adjacent to an existing Rental Car Garage to the West and the existing ATCT to the South.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project consists of Junction Road from Dixie Highway (POB) to Dehmel Road  Block Road to Reese Road (POE)  and Genesee Street from Dehmel Road to Block Road. The total project length is 6.90 miles. For Junction Road  the project includes 3.5 inches of HMA overlay  6 foot paved shoulders placed over the existing gravel shoulders  permanent pavement markings  and driveway improvements. For Genesee Street  the project includes HMA cold milling  2 inches of HMA resurfacing  permanent pavement markings  and sidewalk ramp reconstruction to ADA compliance. Junction Road typically consists of 11 foot lanes with 6 foot gravel shoulders. The proposed cross section for Junction Road typically consists of 11 foot lanes with 6 foot paved shoulders. Genesee Street typically consists of two 12' lanes  a 10' turn lane  and two 4' bike lines either side of the roadway. The proposed cross section for Genesee Street typically consists of two 12' lanes  a 10' turn lane  and two 4' bike lines either side of the roadway. Roadway slopes will tie into the existing ground  or curb  where it is present. All roadwork will be confined within the existing road ROW. There will not be a need for ROW acquisition. Any disturbed areas will be restored by seeding and mulching.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Junction Road: Dixie Highway to Dehmel Road  Block Road to Reese Road; Genesee Street: Dehmel Road to Block Road

The project includes full-depth road reconstruction and will include the intersections at Norton Avenue and Bonneville Drive. The road reconstruction will consist of 6-inches of HMA  8-inches of aggregate base  and 12-inches of sand subbasse for a total road cut of approximately 26-inches. The existing road typically consists of three 12 foot lanes and 4 foot paved shoulders. The proposed cross section will typically consist of three 12 foot lanes and 4 foot paved shoulders. Areas with curb and gutter will be replaced and sidewalk ramps will be upgraded to be ADA compliant. Sidewalk and curb and gutter will be replaced in-kind. This project will include drainage improvements. Additional catch basins may be added to better facilitate drainage and any existing structures that are brick and block will be removed and replaced with pre-cast concrete structures. The existing 10-inch water main will be replaced with a 12-inch water main. All water services will be replaced from the main to the ROW. The sidewalk on both sides of McCracken will be retained  except for patches in poor condition or sections within water service replacement impacts. All permanent signs will be replaced with new sign supports  roadway slopes will be tied into the existing ground  and any disturbed areas will be restored by seeding and mulching. All road and utility work will be contained within the road ROW and previously disturbed soils.nnThe existing 10-inch water main in the SB through lane was installed in 1991. The existing sanitary sewer along the centerline of McCracken Street (Lawnel Boulevard to Southwood Avenue) was installed from 2005-2008. McCracken Street was widened in 1998.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project area consists of 7 Mile Road from Erickson Road (POB) to Pinconning Road (POE). The total project length is 3.92 miles. The project includes HMA base crushing and shaping (estimated 7 inch depth)  HMA resurfacing  shoulder improvements  drainage improvements  slope restoration  and permanent pavement markings. The existing road typically consists of 11 foot lanes and 5 foot gravel shoulders. The proposed section consists of 11 foot lanes  3 foot paved shoulders  and 1 foot gravel shoulders. Roadway slopes will tie into the existing ground. Drainage improvements will be included to facilitate positive drainage. The existing box culvert at Johnson Drain will be retained but will include removal and repair of the headwalls. Two existing cross culverts under the road will be removed and replaced; all other cross culverts will be retained but will include removing the headwalls and extending the culvert ends. The existing storm sewer will be retained and extended as needed. Additionally  the guardrail at the Pinconning River bridge will be removed and replaced. All roadwork will be contained within the existing road ROW. There will not be a need for ROW acquisition. Any disturbed areas will be restored by seeding and mulching. The ground disturbing activities on this project include HMA base crushing and shaping  slope restoration  and new guardrail posts from the POB to the POE.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: 7 Mile Road from Erickson Road to Pinconning Road

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project area consists of E Main Street from Ionia City Limits (POB) to 2nd Street (POE). The total project length is 0.65 miles. All roadwork will be contained within the existing road ROW. There will not be a need for ROW acquisition. PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: In September and October 2024  the USDA APHIS Wildlife Service conducted a site visit to observe and remove wildlife from Airport property.  The USDA APHIS Wildlife Service issued a letter to summarize their efforts and findings.  The report notated multiple areas of concern on the East side of the airfield where the fence line was damaged and needed repair.  Based on current NCDOT Division of Aviation (NCDOA)  FAA  and USDA guidance  it is recommended that new wildlife perimeter fence at airports be 10-foot chain link fence (above ground)  with three (3) strand of barbed wire  and include a wildlife skirt buried below ground to deter wildlife from entering Airport property.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: BE&K-Hitt is requesting a determination for temporary construction cranes to construct a second Final Assembly Building (FAB) for Boeing at their aerospace campus located at 5400 International Blvd in North Charleston South Carolina.  The new/second FAB will be of a similar shape and size and be located approximately 300-feet south of the current/existing FAB.  The building will be constructed in an area that is currently an asphalt parking lot  flat  and has an existing elevation of 16 feet (NAVD-88).  A Final Determination for the building itself was issued via ASN 2024-ASO-15457-NRA.  nnConstruction of the FAB will require use of cranes up to 395' high.  A crane box has been established for this submittal with the location and elevation of the four (4) perimeter corners being consistent with the included Class 1A survey.nRelative to Charleston International Airport (CHS)  the closest edges of the crane box will be 5 000 feet (0.95-miles) southeast of the threshold of Runway 03 and 5 900 feet (1.12 miles) south of the threshold of Runway 33.  The crane box is also 1 200 feet (0.23 miles) west of Interstate 526.nnIt should be noted that the location is deemed "On Airport" since the property is leased to Boeing by an affiliate of Charleston International Airport.nConstruction of the FAB will require use of cranes up to 395' high to erect the steel framing  150' man-lifts  and 150' high-lift fork-lifts to install the exterior cladding  roofing system  lighting  painting and misc. finishes all operating inside the crane box outlined below and in the attached 1A Survey.nnThe FAB building is approximately 600' wide and 1000' long with the center axis-oriented N-S.  The crane box is established 90 feet beyond / outside of the west  north and east sides and 210 feet beyond the south side.nnThe application entered the tallest crane height of 395 feet at each corner of the box  however  the variation in crane height and duration of use is further described as follows:nn-	Beginning January 1st  2026  through December 7th  2026  telehandlers operating at 225' AGL will be on site. PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This project at Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport encompasses the preparation of approximately 65 acres of airfield property for future aviation-related development. Located in the northeast corner of the airport  the project site includes an existing stormwater detention facility and a previously used stockpile area. The objective of this project is to develop a grading and drainage strategy that brings the site to airfield-compatible elevations  manages stormwater runoff in compliance with regulatory requirements  and supports future infrastructure investments. The project will also establish a new access roadway connection to East Lake Boulevard. This proposal is for the geotechnical investigation across the project site to assess subsurface conditions and provide design parameters to support future development. To determine the subsurface conditions  the geotechnical firm proposes to perform 20 soil borings and multiple test pits distributed in a grid pattern.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The site is located in the area northeast of the intersection of Runway 18/36 and Runway 6/24 and south of E Lake Blvd.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The equipment is a crawler crane (LR type) designed for heavy lifting operations. It is mounted on a tracked undercarriage  which provides stability and mobility across various terrain conditions. The crane will be configured with a main boom and an additional luffing jib (luffer) attachment to extend operational flexibility. The crawler undercarriage distributes ground pressure evenly  allowing safe movement and positioning on site. The main boom provides primary lifting capability and is engineered for heavy-duty performance  while the luffing jib enhances reach and versatility  enabling lifting operations at variable radii and angles. A modular counterweight system ensures stability during lifting operations  and the crane is intended for construction and industrial tasks requiring long reach and high capacity. This crane will be used for steel erection.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The lower roadway level (arrivals) roadway would be located at or near existing terminal roadway grade and would include curbside and bypass travel lanes. The upper roadway (departures) level would be constructed above the lower roadway level and would consist of a 9-lane elevated roadway structure supported by structural elements associated with the proposed terminal headhouse and roadway support structures. The upper level roadway elevation is linked to the future upper level terminal headhouse.nThe proposed terminal roadway system would be located within the existing terminal area development footprint. The reported structure height reflects a conservative 15-foot vertical vehicle clearance envelope above the roadway surface. The maximum height of the proposed upper level roadway structure  measured from ground level to the top of the assumed vehicle clearance envelope above the roadway surface  would be 41 feet above ground level (AGL)  with site elevations varying across the project area. Specific elevations and heights are provided in the submitted geographic coordinate points.nConstruction is anticipated to begin around October 2027 and is expected to be completed by October 2030. Construction equipment  including cranes  may be required during construction activities and will be submitted under a separate notice or under this notice as details become available.nThis notice is being submitted for FAA aeronautical review in accordance with 14 CFR Part 77 to determine potential impacts to navigable airspace and air navigation facilities.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: This proposal encompasses the construction of a permanent  multi-level terminal roadway system located on airport property at Dallas Love Field  Dallas  Texas  adjacent to the passenger terminal facility. The proposed roadway system would consist of two roadway levels  abutting the planned future terminal headhouse and serving the future terminal curbside areas.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This proposal encompasses the construction of a permanent six-level parking garage located on airport property at Dallas Love Field  Dallas  Texas. The proposed structure will have an overall height of 92 feet above ground level (AGL)  which includes approximate 15-foot-tall light standards located on the topmost parking level  with a ground site elevation of 478 feet above mean sea level (AMSL).nnConstruction is anticipated to begin around August 2028 and is expected to be completed by March 2030. Construction equipment  including cranes  may be required during construction activities and will be submitted under a separate notice or under this notice as details become available.nThis notice is being submitted for FAA aeronautical review in accordance with 14 CFR Part 77 to determine potential impacts to navigable airspace and air navigation facilities.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The structure is proposed to be located approximately 1 040 feet southwest of the Runway 13L-31R centerline. This distance represents the shortest horizontal separation between the garage facade and the runway centerline. The proposed parking structure would be located immediately adjacent to the existing Garage C parking structure  along the terminal roadway Herb Kelleher Way  and is intended to support passenger parking operations at the Airport.

No new construction or additions are planned; the intent is strictly to address existing issues.nnThis project will not require any crane equipment  as the material used should not exceed a weight where that is necessary.
